chunks: And it is narrated from Al-Bazanti, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sa‘d Al-Khaffaf, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:
We were with him, eight men, and we mentioned Ramadan, so he said:

Do not say, 'This is Ramadan,' nor, 'Ramadan has gone,' nor, 'Ramadan has come,' for Ramadan is a name from among the Names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It does not come and it does not go; rather, that which comes and goes is the passing thing. But say, 'The Month of Ramadan,' for the month is ascribed to the name, and the name is the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and it is the month
"in which the Qur'an was sent down"
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it a symbol and a celebration.

key_terms.أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ: the Names of Allah; divine names carrying sanctity and reverence
key_terms.الزَّائِلُ: that which passes away; the transient thing that comes and goes
key_terms.الْقُرْآنُ: the Qur'an; the revelation sent down in this month
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: Ramadan; presented here as a Name associated with Allah عزّ وجلّ
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan; the proper expression taught in the hadith
key_terms.عِيدًا: a festival or celebration; indicating honored sacred occasion
key_terms.مَثَلًا: a sign or exemplar; something set forth with special significance

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام instruct believers to say 'Shahr Ramadan' instead of simply 'Ramadan'?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches proper reverence in referring to the Month of Ramadan, instructing believers to say 'Shahr Ramadan' rather than speaking of Ramadan itself as coming or going. It presents Ramadan as one of the Names of Allah عزّ وجلّ and connects the blessed month to the Qur'an's revelation and its honored, festive status.
